apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-01.question: In Revelation 2:4, Jesus says Ephesus abandoned its first love.
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus praises the church but points out the loss of its first love.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Revelation 2:4 and see what the church left behind.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-02.question: In Revelation 2:4, tap what Ephesus left behind.
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-02.feedbackCorrect: The church left its first love, and Jesus calls it back.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the start of the speech, not what was left behind.
feedbackWrong.c: That introduces the rebuke; it doesn't say what was left.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-02.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-03.question: According to Revelation 2:10, what does Jesus promise to those faithful until death?
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-03.feedbackCorrect: The promise to the faithful who suffer is the crown of life given by Jesus.

feedbackWrong.a: Smyrna is poor outwardly; the promised wealth is different.
feedbackWrong.b: The promise cited is the crown of life, not an earthly throne.
feedbackWrong.d: The text speaks of tribulation and prison, not absence of suffering.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: Wealth on this earth
options.b: A place among kings
options.c: The crown of life
options.d: A life without suffering

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-04.question: Put Revelation 2:7 in the order of the text.
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-04.feedbackCorrect: First the call to listen, then the promise to the one who overcomes.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the call to listen; the tree of life comes after.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-04.hint: The verse begins by calling us to listen.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-05.question: In Revelation 2:10, what will Jesus give to those faithful until death?
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-05.feedbackCorrect: To the faithful until death, Jesus promises the crown of life.

feedbackWrong.b: Prison is the trial mentioned earlier, not Jesus' gift.
feedbackWrong.c: Death is the limit of faithfulness, not what Jesus gives.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-05.hint: Look for the gift promised at the end.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-06.question: What does Revelation 2:7 convey that connects to this context?
apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-06.feedbackCorrect: Whoever listens and overcomes eats from the tree of life in God's paradise.

feedbackWrong.a: The promise is life in paradise, not immediate wealth.
feedbackWrong.b: Smyrna would still suffer; the promise is not escape from trial.

apocalipse-sem-apo-01-cartas-06.hint: Look at what is given to the one who overcomes.

options.a: Wealth without perseverance
options.b: Escape from every trial
options.c: Life for the one who overcomes

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-01.question: In Revelation 2:5, Jesus waives repentance for those who return to their first works.
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-01.feedbackCorrect: The way back goes through remembering, repenting, and practicing again.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Revelation 2:5 and see the steps Jesus asks for.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-01.hint: Look at the verbs Jesus uses.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-02.question: In Revelation 2:6, tap the word that marks the contrast with the previous rebuke.
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-02.feedbackCorrect: After the rebuke, Jesus also acknowledges a good point in Ephesus.

feedbackWrong.a: That word only picks up the works mentioned.
feedbackWrong.b: That word links Jesus to the church, but doesn't open the contrast.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-02.hint: Look for the short word after the opening comma.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-03.question: How does Revelation 2:5 respond to the problem pointed out in Revelation 2:4?
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-03.feedbackCorrect: The answer to the loss of love is to remember, repent, and return to the first works.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus corrects the same church; he doesn't replace it there.
feedbackWrong.b: The coming announced is soon if there is no repentance.
feedbackWrong.d: Jesus says to remember where you fell from, not to forget.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-03.hint: Compare the problem of 2:4 with the verbs of 2:5.

options.a: Swaps the church for a more faithful one
options.b: Postpones the correction to the end times
options.c: Calls to remember, repent, and act in love again
options.d: Tells us to forget the past and go on unchanged

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-04.question: How does Jesus' speech to Ephesus progress in Revelation 2:4–7?
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-04.feedbackCorrect: First the diagnosis, then the call, and finally the promise.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the problem pointed out; the promise closes the letter.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-04.hint: The promise to the one who overcomes comes last.

options.a: Jesus points out the loss of the first love
options.b: He calls them to remember and repent
options.c: He promises life to the one who overcomes

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-05.question: In Revelation 2:5, what is the step between remembering and returning to the first works?
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-05.feedbackCorrect: Remembering leads to repenting, and only then to returning to the first works.

feedbackWrong.a: Complacency is the opposite of the repentance asked for.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus says to remember, not to forget where you fell from.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-05.hint: It is the central verb of the verse.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-06.question: What connects Revelation 2:10 to James 1:12?
apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, whoever perseveres and is approved receives the crown of life.

feedbackWrong.a: James calls blessed the one who endures trial.
feedbackWrong.b: In both texts the promise comes after the trial is endured.

apocalipse-cam-apo-01-cartas-06.hint: Compare the final promise in both passages.

options.a: Prison with no purpose at all
options.b: Victory without any trial
options.c: Crown of life for the faithful

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-01.question: In Revelation 2:9, Jesus treats Smyrna as poor outwardly but rich before him.
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-01.feedbackCorrect: In human eyes there is poverty; in Jesus' eyes, the faithful church is rich.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the parenthesis of Revelation 2:9 about Smyrna's poverty.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-01.hint: Notice the contrast within the verse.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-02.question: In Revelation 2:7, tap the part with the promise made to the one who overcomes.
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-02.feedbackCorrect: The promise to the one who overcomes is to eat from the tree of life in God's paradise.

feedbackWrong.a: That says whom the Spirit speaks to, not what is promised.
feedbackWrong.b: That is the call to listen, not the promise.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-02.hint: Look for what the one who overcomes receives.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-03.question: What reading does Revelation 2:4–5 support about a church that is active but loveless?
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus joins both things: returning to love and to the first works, with repentance.

feedbackWrong.a: He says he has something against the church for this loss.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus rebukes precisely the loss of the first love.
feedbackWrong.c: He tells them to return to the first works, not abandon them.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-03.hint: See the remedy Jesus gives for the problem.

options.a: Jesus ignores lack of love if there are works
options.b: Activity is enough, even without love in the heart
options.c: The church must abandon works in order to love
options.d: Losing the first love calls for repentance and return

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the one who overcomes in Revelation 2?
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-04.feedbackCorrect: Listening leads to repentance and faithfulness, and God gives the promise of life.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by listening to the Spirit; the promise is the point of arrival.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-04.hint: Follow the order: listen, remain, receive.

options.a: The church hears what the Spirit says
options.b: The faithful repents and remains to the end
options.c: The one who overcomes receives the promise of life

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-05.question: In Revelation 2:7, whom should the church listen to carefully?
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-05.feedbackCorrect: The call is to listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.

feedbackWrong.a: Ears are who should listen, not who speaks.
feedbackWrong.c: The churches are the ones who listen; the one who speaks is another.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-05.hint: See who says something to the churches.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-06.question: What connects Revelation 2:7 to Revelation 22:2?
apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-06.feedbackCorrect: The tree promised to the one who overcomes reappears in the new creation, healing the nations.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts the tree is where God dwells with his people.
feedbackWrong.b: The promise of 2:7 is fulfilled at the end of the book, in 22:2.

apocalipse-pro-apo-01-cartas-06.hint: Compare the tree mentioned in both passages.

options.a: Life far from paradise
options.b: A promise only for the past
options.c: Tree of life restored

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-01.question: In Revelation 5:6, John sees a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain.
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-01.feedbackCorrect: The Lamb stands, alive, yet marked by the death he suffered.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Revelation 5:6 and see whom John sees in the midst of the throne.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-01.hint: See who appears in the midst of the throne.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-02.question: In Revelation 5:6, tap whom John saw in the midst of the throne.
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-02.feedbackCorrect: At the center of the throne is the Lamb standing, as though slain.

feedbackWrong.a: The elders are around it; in the middle is another.
feedbackWrong.c: The living creatures surround the throne; the center belongs to another.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-02.hint: Look for the center of the scene.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-03.question: According to Revelation 5:8, what are the golden bowls full of incense?
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-03.feedbackCorrect: The text itself explains that the incense is the prayers of the saints.

feedbackWrong.a: Songs come with harps; the bowls are something else.
feedbackWrong.b: The text doesn't link the bowls to tears, but to prayers.
feedbackWrong.d: The text calls the bowls the prayers of the saints.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-03.hint: Read the explanation at the end of the verse.

options.a: The songs of the angels
options.b: The tears of the martyrs
options.c: The prayers of the saints
options.d: The offerings of the churches

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-04.question: Put Revelation 5:9 in the order of the text.
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-04.feedbackCorrect: The song begins, declares the Lamb worthy, and says why.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the song; the reason for his worthiness comes at the end.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-04.hint: The verse begins with the song.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-05.question: In Revelation 5:12, what is the last word of the praise to the Lamb?
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-05.feedbackCorrect: The list of praise to the Lamb ends with the final word of the verse.

feedbackWrong.b: That word comes before the last one in the list.
feedbackWrong.c: That word opens the list, not closes it.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-05.hint: See the last word of the list.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-06.question: What does Revelation 5:9 convey that connects to this context?
apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-06.feedbackCorrect: Those bought by the blood come from every tribe, language, people, and nation.

feedbackWrong.a: The text opens the purchase to all nations.
feedbackWrong.c: In 5:13, every creature joins in the praise.

apocalipse-sem-apo-02-cordeiro-06.hint: See the origin of those bought.

options.a: Salvation for a single people
options.b: Salvation for all nations
options.c: Praise only from angels

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-01.question: In Revelation 5:8, the elders fall down before the Lamb when he takes the scroll.
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-01.feedbackCorrect: On taking the scroll, the Lamb receives the worship of the living creatures and elders.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Revelation 5:8 and see the reaction to the scroll being taken.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-01.hint: See what happens when the scroll is taken.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-02.question: In Revelation 5:8, tap the part that explains what the incense is.
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-02.feedbackCorrect: The incense in the bowls is the prayers of the saints before the Lamb.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the container; the explanation comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: The harp accompanies the praise; it doesn't explain the incense.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-02.hint: Look for the explanation at the end of the verse.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-03.question: How does Revelation 5:9 explain why the Lamb can open the seals?
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-03.feedbackCorrect: The Lamb's worthiness comes from his death, which bought people for God.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no dispute; there is unanimous praise to the Lamb.
feedbackWrong.c: He takes the scroll openly from the hand of the one on the throne.
feedbackWrong.d: The song speaks not of age, but of redeeming death.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-03.hint: Look for the reason after the word worthy.

options.a: He was slain and bought people for God with his blood
options.b: He defeated the elders in a heavenly contest
options.c: He received the scroll hidden from the others
options.d: He is the oldest being in all creation

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-04.question: How does the scene progress in Revelation 5:6–9?
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-04.feedbackCorrect: First the Lamb appears, then takes the scroll, and then comes the song.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the Lamb's appearance; the song comes after the scroll.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-04.hint: The song responds to the scroll being taken.

options.a: The Lamb appears in the midst of the throne
options.b: The Lamb takes the scroll from the throne
options.c: Heaven sings the new song

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-05.question: In Revelation 5:9, with what did the Lamb buy people for God?
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-05.feedbackCorrect: It was with his blood that the Lamb bought people from all nations.

feedbackWrong.a: The scroll is what the Lamb takes, not the price of the purchase.
feedbackWrong.b: The seals are opened on the scroll; they are not the price paid.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-05.hint: See the price mentioned in the song.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-06.question: What connects Revelation 5:9 to John 1:29?
apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-06.feedbackCorrect: John the Baptist announces the Lamb of God; on the throne, he buys the nations.

feedbackWrong.b: In both texts the Lamb truly acts for the world.
feedbackWrong.c: In Revelation he buys people from every nation with his blood.

apocalipse-cam-apo-02-cordeiro-06.hint: Compare the title given to Jesus in both passages.

options.a: Lamb who takes away sin
options.b: A merely symbolic lamb
options.c: Sacrifice with no effect on the world

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-01.question: In Revelation 5:9, the Lamb is worthy because he won by force without needing to be slain.
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-01.feedbackCorrect: The Lamb's worthiness comes through his death and his blood.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the reason the song gives in Revelation 5:9.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-01.hint: See the reason sung in heaven.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-02.question: In Revelation 5:9, tap the part that supports the Lamb's worthiness.
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-02.feedbackCorrect: Heaven calls the Lamb worthy because he was slain for us.

feedbackWrong.b: That shows the reach of the purchase, not its foundation.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the form of the praise, not the reason for his worthiness.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-02.hint: Look for the reason after the declaration of worthiness.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-03.question: What reading does Revelation 5:9–10 support about whom the Lamb saved?
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-03.feedbackCorrect: Those bought come from all nations and are made kings and priests for God.

feedbackWrong.b: The text lists every tribe, language, people, and nation.
feedbackWrong.c: The one who buys is the Lamb, with his blood, not the saved.
feedbackWrong.d: The angels sing; those bought are people from the nations.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-03.hint: See the origin and destiny of those bought.

options.a: People from all nations made God's people
options.b: Only one chosen nation among the others
options.c: Those who managed to buy their own salvation
options.d: Only the angels who sing in heaven

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the Lamb's victory?
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-04.feedbackCorrect: From the Lamb's death is born a people from all nations for God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the Lamb's death; the reign of his people comes after.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-04.hint: Follow the order: death, purchase, reign.

options.a: The Lamb is slain for his people
options.b: People from every nation are bought for God
options.c: Those bought reign as God's people

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-05.question: In Revelation 5:10, those bought were made kings and what else?
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-05.feedbackCorrect: The people bought are made kings and priests for God.

feedbackWrong.b: Angels are other beings in the throne scene.
feedbackWrong.c: Elders worship in the scene; those bought receive another role.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-05.hint: See the second role given to those bought.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-06.question: What connects Revelation 5:6 to Isaiah 53:7?
apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah announces the servant as a lamb led to slaughter; John sees him standing on the throne.

feedbackWrong.a: The Lamb's victory comes precisely from his surrender unto death.
feedbackWrong.b: In both texts the Lamb goes through suffering and death.

apocalipse-pro-apo-02-cordeiro-06.hint: Compare the lamb figure in both passages.

options.a: Victory without any surrender
options.b: A king who never suffers
options.c: Lamb led to death

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-01.question: In Revelation 21:4, God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-01.feedbackCorrect: In the new creation, God himself wipes away every tear from his people.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Revelation 21:4 and see God's gesture.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-02.question: In Revelation 21:2, tap the name of the city coming down from heaven.
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-02.feedbackCorrect: The city coming down from heaven, from God, is the new Jerusalem.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the comparison of the adorned city, not its name.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the city, but the name comes next.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-02.hint: Look for the city's proper name.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-03.question: According to Revelation 21:4, what will no longer exist in the new creation?
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-03.feedbackCorrect: Death, mourning, crying, and pain pass away with the former things.

feedbackWrong.b: God's people will be with him in the new creation.
feedbackWrong.c: God will dwell with mankind; he will not be absent.
feedbackWrong.d: The new Jerusalem comes down precisely to this new world.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-03.hint: Read the list of what ends.

options.a: Death and pain
options.b: God's people
options.c: God's presence
options.d: The holy city

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-04.question: Put Revelation 21:3 in the order of the text.
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-04.feedbackCorrect: God dwells with mankind, they are his people, and he is their God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God's tabernacle with mankind.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-04.hint: The verse begins with the tabernacle.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-05.question: In Revelation 21:1, John sees a new heaven and what kind of earth?
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-05.feedbackCorrect: John sees a new heaven and a new earth made by God.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of newness, not of old age.
feedbackWrong.b: The first earth is the one that already passed away in the verse.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-05.hint: See what the earth is like after the first one.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-06.question: What does Revelation 21:3 convey that connects to this context?
apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-06.feedbackCorrect: The heart of the new creation is God dwelling with his people.

feedbackWrong.a: They will be his people, and he will be their God.
feedbackWrong.c: The voice from the throne announces precisely God's presence.

apocalipse-sem-apo-03-novo-06.hint: Listen to the voice coming from the throne.

options.a: A people without God present
options.b: God dwelling with his people
options.c: God far from his people

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-01.question: In Revelation 21:4, the former things keep bringing mourning and pain forever.
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-01.feedbackCorrect: The former things have passed away, and with them death, mourning, and pain.
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-01.hint: See the fate of the former things.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-02.question: In Revelation 21:3, tap the verb that says what God will do with mankind.
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-02.feedbackCorrect: God doesn't just visit in passing: he will dwell with his people.

feedbackWrong.a: That says what mankind will be, not what God will do.
feedbackWrong.b: That reinforces his presence, but the main action comes earlier.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-03.question: How does Revelation 21:2 present the arrival of the new Jerusalem?
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-03.feedbackCorrect: The city is a gift from God coming down, not a work built by people.

feedbackWrong.b: The text says it comes down from heaven, not up from the earth.
feedbackWrong.c: The sea no longer exists in the new creation of 21:1.
feedbackWrong.d: John sees it coming down from God, not merely dreaming it.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-03.hint: See where the city comes from.

options.a: It comes down from heaven, from God
options.b: It rises from the earth, built by people
options.c: It emerges from the sea after the final battle
options.d: It appears only in John's dreams

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-04.question: How does the scene progress in Revelation 21:1–4?
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-04.feedbackCorrect: First the new world, then the city coming down, and then God with his people.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the new heaven and new earth; God with his people comes after.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-04.hint: God dwelling with his people is the high point.

options.a: A new heaven and a new earth appear
options.b: The holy city comes down from God
options.c: God dwells and wipes away the tears

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-05.question: In Revelation 21:5, what does God say he does with all things?
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-05.feedbackCorrect: The one on the throne declares that he makes all things new.

feedbackWrong.b: God renews; he doesn't make all things old.
feedbackWrong.c: The former things are the ones that have already passed away.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-05.hint: Hear the declaration of the one on the throne.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-06.question: What connects Revelation 21:1 to Isaiah 65:17?
apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah already announced a new heaven and a new earth; John sees them arriving.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts God creates something new; he doesn't leave everything the same.
feedbackWrong.b: It is a renewal of creation, not its total disappearance.

apocalipse-cam-apo-03-novo-06.hint: Compare what God creates in the passages.

options.a: Same earth without change
options.b: End of all creation
options.c: New heaven and new earth

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-01.question: In Revelation 21:5, the one on the throne says he makes all things new.
apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-01.feedbackCorrect: The renewal of everything is the word of the one seated on the throne.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Revelation 21:5 and see who speaks.

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-01.hint: Listen to the one on the throne.

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-02.question: In Revelation 21:4, tap the part that shows God's personal comfort.
apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-02.feedbackCorrect: God himself wipes every tear from the eyes of his people.

feedbackWrong.a: That explains why the pain ends, not the gesture of comfort.
feedbackWrong.c: That speaks of the death that ends, not of God's gesture.

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-02.hint: Look for what God wipes away.

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-03.question: What reading does Revelation 21:3–4 support about the future of God's people?
apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-03.feedbackCorrect: The future is full communion: God with his people, without tears or death.

feedbackWrong.a: God will dwell with them and be their God.
feedbackWrong.b: God wipes away the tears; the pain doesn't go on hidden.
feedbackWrong.c: They will be his people, gathered together with him.

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-03.hint: Put together God's presence and the end of pain.

options.a: God distant, and his people alone forever
options.b: Pain continues, only hidden from God
options.c: The people stop being a people and live isolated
options.d: God present with his people, without death or pain

apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path to the new creation?
apocalipse-pro-apo-03-novo-04.feedbackCorrect: From the God who created everything to the God who renews everything at the end.
